newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon court gets documents on election appeals.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon court gets documents on election appeals.

text.p: Lebanon's Constitutional Council on Friday received a mountain of documents needed to rule on 19 appeals from defeated candidates against the results of recent parliamentary elections.
The interior ministry, which organized the vote marred by accusations of voting by dead people and vote-buying, handed the documents to the court hours before the deadline, officials said.
"There are more than 40,000 documents," the ministry's director-general Atallah Ghashaam was quoted saying by Lebanon's official National News Agency.
Eighteen defeated candidates lodged appeals demanding the council overturn the results of individual races and declare them winners, and one demanded cancellation of the entire election.
Syrian-backed government supporters won an overwhelming majority of parliament's 128 seats in the five-stage elections which ended on September 15.
The 10-member Constitutional Council can cancel the election of individual deputies and award their seats to other candidates if it decides serious fraud existed.
